medium.title: Optimistic Markets Ahead of Employment Data; Ibovespa in Dollar Terms Rises Today (June 30)
medium.summary: Markets are trading higher on Tuesday following a positive start to the week on Wall Street, with the Ibovespa gaining ground in USD-denominated terms. The rally is being driven by improved investor sentiment amid signs of geopolitical stability and anticipation of upcoming U.S. economic data — specifically, the U.S. jobs report, a key macro catalyst for global risk appetite. Notably, technology stocks led gains on Monday, helping the Dow Jones Industrial Average close at a record high. Additionally, a U.S. Supreme Court ruling reinforcing the independence of the Federal Reserve appears to have provided further market support. For BRL and Ibovespa traders, this is a meaningful short-term signal: a constructive global risk environment typically supports capital flows into emerging markets, putting mild upward pressure on the BRL and Brazilian equities. Watch the U.S. payrolls print closely — a weaker-than-expected number could fuel Fed rate cut expectations, further boosting EM assets including BRL and B3.

medium.title: EU Tightens Rules and Imposes 50% Tariff on Excess Steel Imports
medium.summary: The European Commission announced a 47% reduction in the annual steel quota eligible for tariff-free entry into the EU, capping imports at 18.3 million tonnes per year across 26 steel product categories, effective July 1st. Shipments exceeding this threshold will face a 50% tariff. This development carries indirect relevance for Brazilian markets, particularly for steel-linked equities and exporters. Brazil is a significant steel exporter, and tighter EU safeguards could divert Brazilian steel volumes — pressuring margins for domestic producers with European exposure. More broadly, escalating trade protectionism in key markets adds a layer of uncertainty to Brazil's trade balance outlook, which in turn has implications for the BRL's medium-term direction. Investors with exposure to Brazilian steel and metals should monitor how domestic producers respond to rerouted trade flows.

medium.title: Warsh's Comments Could Shake Market Bets; Ibovespa in Dollar Terms Falls Today (1st)
medium.summary: As investors kick off the second half of 2026, market attention is focused on remarks from Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh at the Sintra monetary policy forum, where he is joined by ECB President Christine Lagarde and Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey. The article notes that the market is actively recalibrating U.S. interest rate expectations, and Warsh's tone — whether hawkish or dovish — could have direct implications for emerging market assets including the BRL and the Ibovespa measured in USD terms. A more hawkish Fed stance typically strengthens the USD, pressuring the BRL and increasing outflows from Brazilian equities and fixed income. The headline explicitly flags that the Ibovespa in dollar terms is declining on this date, suggesting early risk-off sentiment. Fund managers should monitor Warsh's commentary closely for signals on the pace of U.S. rate adjustments, as any shift in Fed guidance will directly influence BRL/USD dynamics and the attractiveness of Brazilian government bonds relative to U.S. Treasuries heading into Q3 2026.

medium.title: Eurozone Inflation Decelerates More Than Expected, Reducing Pressure on the ECB
medium.summary: Eurozone headline inflation fell to 2.8% in June from 3.2% in May, coming in well below the consensus estimate of 3.0%, with food, energy, and services price increases all decelerating. This softer-than-expected print reduces pressure on the ECB to raise rates further, reinforcing a "patient" stance among policymakers gathered at the Sintra forum. While this is a European data point, it carries indirect relevance for Brazilian markets: a more dovish ECB reduces global risk-off pressure and can modestly support emerging market currencies including the BRL, while also influencing the broader DXY dynamic that drives USD/BRL. Combined with the Sintra panel featuring Warsh, Lagarde, and Bailey simultaneously, the global monetary policy backdrop on July 1st is a key driver of short-term sentiment for BRL and Ibovespa flows.
